edits.old: Roth contributions pay tax now and skip it later.
edits.new: Roth contributions are after-tax. Earnings are tax-free only on a qualified distribution after five tax years of participation and age 59½, death or disability. Native governmental 457(b) penalty treatment does not by itself make Roth earnings tax-free.

edits.old: First, California's brackets bite early. A single filer sits in the 9.3% marginal bracket starting around $73,000 of taxable income, and that bracket runs all the way to roughly $371,000 (2025 figures from third-party transcriptions of the FTB rate schedules; the official 2026 bracket dollars publish in fall 2026, so treat the exact cutoffs as approximate until then). Practically, that means nearly every overtime dollar a mid-career firefighter earns gets taxed at 9.3% by the state on top of federal tax.
edits.new: For 2026, a single or married/RDP separate filer enters California's 9.3% marginal bracket above $75,197 of taxable income, through $384,109. The standard deduction is $5,900 for single or separate filers and $11,800 for joint, surviving-spouse or head-of-household filers. Use the FTB's 2026 figures and taxable income, rather than gross salary, for a same-year comparison.

edits.old: Ask questions at the right time. Not during a call, not when the officer is busy, not in the middle of a task. Save them for downtime and make them good questions that show you were paying attention.
edits.new: Ask questions when they are needed. Raise an immediate hazard, unclear assignment or patient-safety concern promptly through your crew's procedures. Save nonurgent learning questions for a suitable pause or downtime.
